text:
Maya K: FYI I'm seeing a repeat of last week's IOPS spike on the tempstore NVMe pool in us-west2 during the 03:00 janitor window. GPU attach times jumped 10-30s for a handful of launches.
Devon: same pattern seen in eu-west2-scratch yesterday. Looks like a read/write amplification wave after the scrub.
oncall-bot: ALERT nvme_io_surge: hostpool-usw2-tempstore group=janitor concurrency=8 iops=~120k
Maya K: logs from the attach agent show `IO_TIMEOUT` retries when mounts hit the local device for >150ms. stacktrace lines: `attach_manager.go:182` `nvme_probe.go:77`
Sam Ops: quick ask — can we throttle janitor concurrency to 2 for the us-west2 tempstore? I can push a config change if folks agree.
Li: smart data shows older firmware on a subset (Model X123, fw 1.0.3) with wear_level trending +6% in last 7d. That cohort correlates with the highest amplification.
Devon: could be the janitor's deep-scrub doing full-pass rewrite after partial GC. If the scrub hits many small files it creates a lot of random writes.
Maya K: repro steps from one host:
```
# observe io
iotop -o -b -n 2
# janitor job id
jq '.job_id' /var/log/janitor/current.json
# attach failure
cat /var/log/attach/attach.log | tail -n 50
```
Sam Ops: rolling the throttle now to `janitor.concurrent=2` for tempstore-us-west2 in the feature flags. Pushing change to infra-config map -> kube rollout.
Sam Ops: `kubectl -n infra rollout restart deploy/janitor-worker --selector=pool=tempstore-us-west2` (started) :hourglass:
oncall-bot: CHANGELOG change: janitor.concurrent=2 applied to tempstore-us-west2 by Sam Ops at 2026-03-20T03:12:05Z
Devon: as a medium-term mitigation we should route GPU provisioning to fallback scratchpool-hot for 10m when nvme_iops > 80k to avoid attach backoffs. Can we add a policy to the routing layer?
Maya K: +1 — that will buy headroom while we investigate root cause.
Li: I'll open a hardware ticket for the X123 cohort and request firmware 1.0.6 test devices. Also rework scrub job to use read-only verification where possible (avoid rewrite).
Devon: for diagnostics I pushed a short eval that runs `fio` microbench on a staging node to characterize R/W mix impact. link: https://console.redwood/internal/dashboards/io/fio-test?run=20260320-1
Sam Ops: I've scheduled a canary of the routing policy to flip in 5m. Will monitor attach latency on `provision-trace` dashboard.
Maya K: Monitoring note — add an alert to trigger when `tempstore.iops.1m > 80k` AND `gpu.attach.p50 > 2s` so we can auto-fallback routing.
Devon: Also let's add a daily low-concurrency scrub window instead of single big pass. Patch idea in PR: `scrub.window_size=10m, scrub.concurrency=1`
Li: assigning follow-ups: hardware ticket (Li), routing policy PR (Devon), scrub job rewrite (Maya), permanent throttle roll if stable (Sam Ops).
Maya K: thanks. If anyone sees corruption signatures (checksum fails) call it out here immediately. So far only latency and short-lived attach retries, no fs-level corruptions observed. :thumbsup:
Sam Ops: will revert the throttle if we see regressions. Monitoring configured.
oncall-bot: RESOLVED partial: nvme_io_surge reduced to ~25k iops after throttle change — continuing to monitor.
